# `•element` — XML elements

`•element tag` returns an element function for the XML tag `tag`. The function is displayed as the call that made it, such as `•element"circle"`. Typing that text makes the same function.

Pass only an attributes record to make an element with no children: `circle ["r":10]`. Text, a vector of children or an existing element tree supplies children instead. With both attributes and children, put the attributes on the left, as in `["x":5] text "Hello"`. An empty right argument, `""` or `⍬`, gives no children.

The result is a keyed vector with `tag`, `attrs` and `children` entries. Notebooks display it as HTML. In that HTML, the text of a `script` or `style` element isn't escaped, as browsers require. A `script` element can hold JavaScript for the page. [XML and SVG](../xml.ipynb) covers element trees.

Errors: `DOMAIN` for invalid tag or attribute names.
